svg.title: Write locally, run on the cluster
svg.desc: The project repository lives on the laptop disk and is bind mounted into a devcontainer, where a coding agent edits it. xsync runs on the laptop outside the container and watches the repository. The repo is backed up to GitHub. xsync mirrors the repo one way over SSH to a project share on cluster storage. A job container on the cluster mounts the project share and a separate data storage that is shielded: neither the laptop nor the coding agent can reach it. Both containers are pulled from the same image in a container registry, such as Docker Hub. A lower panel shows what one sync does per file: updated, created, removed, and excluded paths.
svg.text: Write locally, run on the cluster
Development workflow with a sandboxed coding agent and one way file mirroring
Image registry, one image for both
Coding agents, sees the repo only
On the laptop disk, outside the container
Watch mode, one way over SSH
The share becomes an exact copy of the repo, minus excluded paths
xsync mirror, seconds after each edit
